note.note:
Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- Young adult female with sudden-onset, severe, persistent headache with visual symptoms and photophobia; probable migraine with aura. Alternative diagnosis (cerebral venous sinus thrombosis) also considered due to risk factors.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Blinding headache for 3 days, started suddenly upon waking; persistently present, partial but incomplete response to ibuprofen.
- Timeline: Began 3 days ago, remains throughout the day and night (not waking patient from sleep, but present in morning).
- Location/features: All-over headache, more intense over right eye.
- Severity: 8/10 at worst, decreases to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia, visual disturbances described as ‘shooting lights’ and "weird vision," mild nausea but no vomiting.
- Pertinent negatives: No past similar severe episodes, no focal neurological deficits (no weakness, numbness, tingling, or speech difficulty), no fever, no neck stiffness, no sinus or upper respiratory symptoms, no smell or taste changes.
- Past medical history: None significant.
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (started ~1 year ago), intermittent ibuprofen use for headache relief.
- Allergies: None reported.
- Family history: Mother has migraine with aura and vomiting.
- Social: Lives alone, works from home but unable to work due to headache; no smoking, moderate alcohol (drinks once weekly), no illicit drug use.
- Preventive health: Blood pressure last checked 1 year ago (normal).

Examination:
- No physical examination performed during this consult.
- No vital signs documented.
- No clinical evidence of neurological deficit reported by patient.
- No signs of infection reported (no fever, neck stiffness, systemic illness).
- Recent eye check was unremarkable.

Impression:
- Working clinical impression: 
    • Migraine with aura (High likelihood—classic features present: severe headache, photophobia, visual aura, family history, no systemic or neurological deficits).
    • Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (Medium likelihood—risk factors present: female, on combined oral contraceptive; features include sudden severe headache, positional worsening, persistent symptoms not relieved with standard analgesia).
    • Subarachnoid hemorrhage and viral meningitis considered less likely due to absence of classic features or systemic signs.
- Rationale: Symptoms fit migraine with aura, but prolonged duration and incomplete relief warrant consideration of alternative/serious secondary causes. No red flags such as focal deficit, altered consciousness, or meningism, but oral contraceptive use and sudden onset require exclusion of cerebral venous sinus thrombosis.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person appointment for neurological examination and fundoscopic (back of eye) examination.
- Prescribe stronger analgesic than ibuprofen and advise concomitant paracetamol use.
- Advise to take medication with food.
- Book appointment via support line for further assessment.
- Advise patient to seek emergency care (A&E) if headache worsens, changes in character, becomes unbearable, or new symptoms (particularly neurological) develop before scheduled appointment.
- On further evaluation, plan to check blood pressure and review appropriateness of current oral contraceptive in context of possible migraine with aura.
- No immediate referral to specialist; to be considered after in-person assessment if necessary.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements:
   - No in-person physical or neurological exam findings documented.
   - Vitals (blood pressure, temperature) not measured at time of consult.
   - No mention of follow-up interval after planned in-person assessment.
   - Full details of current oral contraceptive ("the pill") not specified by name.
● Conflict:
   - None identified; DDx reinforces diagnostic reasoning aligned with transcript evidence.
● Transcript quality:
   - Complete for remote history and safety-netting; physical findings absent (video/telephone only). Occasional minor conversational noise but clinical content clear.
